subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for November 24, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

script.heading: Story 3 - Multidimensional Predictors of Post-Traumatic Stress in Relati
sentences: Story 3 is about Multidimensional Predictors of Post-Traumatic Stress in Relatives of Critically Ill Patients..
This is a recent research article from American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in adults on mechanical ventilation for ≥48 h in 60 ICUs in France (15 December 2022-30 January 2024); for each patient, we enrolled one relative, how should we interpret Exposure or intervention stated in the title/objective. compared with Comparator or control group stated in the methods/results, if present.?
Of 1346 relatives, 936 (69·5%) completed PCL-5 at 3-month: 106 (11·3%) had probable PTSD and 358 (38·2%) clinically relevant post-traumatic stress symptoms.

Factors associated with higher PCL-5 scores included pre-existing characteristics (social exclusion, living alone, perceived disability, and history of psychological trauma), early symptoms (anxiety, peritraumatic dissociation, and insomnia), and greater severity in the patients (vasopressor use and end-of-life decisions).
Lower PCL-5 scores were associated with male sex and specific physician communication behaviours.
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Use as an awareness item; read the full article before applying it clinically.

script.heading: Outro
sentences: That wraps up today's journal club style update.
Before applying any finding, check the full source, the absolute effect size, and your local ICU context.
For English practice, repeat one academic phrase from each article out loud.

articles.title: Subphenotyping and precision medicine approaches to ARDS.
articles.summary: Subphenotyping aims to address this heterogeneity by identifying more homogeneous patient groups that differ in prognosis and/or treatment response. Sixty years after its initial description, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains defined by bilateral radiographic opacities and impaired oxygenation rather than by its underlying biology. This syndromic definition encompasses considerable clinical and biological heterogeneity, which may contribute to the ineffectiveness of pharmacotherapy trials to date. In this narrative review, framed by the research questions outlined in the 2023 European Society of Intensive Care Medicine guidelines, we synthesize current approaches to ARDS subphenotyping across complementary domains: clinical (etiology, rapidly improving ARDS), physiological (gas exchange, recruitability, elastance, and ventilatory ratio), morphological (focal versus non-focal radiological patterns), and biological (individual injury biomarkers and the hyperinflammatory and hypoinflammatory subphenotypes). We examine their pathobiological basis, temporal dynamics, and retrospective evidence for heterogeneity of treatment effect, and consider how parsimonious biomarker panels, machine-learning classifiers, and adaptive basket trial designs may support clinical implementation.

articles.summary: Patients in the AID-ICU were randomized to either haloperidol or placebo (0.9% saline) when treated for delirium in the ICU. articles.title: Multidimensional Predictors of Post-Traumatic Stress in Relatives of Critically Ill Patients.
articles.source: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.summary: Of 1346 relatives, 936 (69·5%) completed PCL-5 at 3-month: 106 (11·3%) had probable PTSD and 358 (38·2%) clinically relevant post-traumatic stress symptoms. Relatives of critically ill patients frequently develop post-traumatic stress symptoms. Few studies have evaluated both psychological and ICU-related risk factors. We aimed to identify factors associated with post-traumatic stress symptom severity and probable post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in ICU relatives. In this prospective multicentre cohort study (FAME), we enrolled consecutive adults on mechanical ventilation for ≥48 h in 60 ICUs in France (15 December 2022-30 January 2024); for each patient, we enrolled one relative.
